classification: Researcher interpretation from scale endpoints and participant instructions; not an author-provided categorical variable.

items.short_description: It was incongruent with your standards and ideas
items.instructions: A situation is congruent with your standards or ideas, if what is happending and how people are acting is in line with your personal values and you would consider it as fair. Move the gauge up the more the situation alignes with your standards and ideas and down if what is happening violates them. You may use the middle of the scale for situations that are neutral with regards to your standards and ideas.
items.note: 补表短说明为不相符，但操作说明明确上端符合、下端违背；据操作说明判为双极。

items.instructions: Pleasant discribes a situation that was generally positive for you. Move the gauge up the more pleasant you perceive the situation and down as the situation is more unpleasant. You may use the middle of the scale for situation that are neither positive or negative.

items.short_description: It violated laws or socially accepted norms
items.instructions: A situation is congruent with social norms,  if what is happening and how people are acting is in line with your cultures expectations regarding social rules and behaviour. Move the gauge up the more the situation is conform with your laws or social norms and down if what is happening violates these ideas. You may use the middle of the scale for situations that are neutral with regards to laws and social norms.
items.note: 下端虽写NotSocialNorms，操作说明明确是违反规范；中间为中性。

items.short_description: It was unpleasant for somebody else
items.instructions: Pleasant for somebody else discribes a situation that you perceive as generally positive for somebody else. Move the gauge up the more pleasant you perceive the situation is for somebody else and down as the situation is more unpleasant for them. You may use the middle of the scale for situation that are neither positive or negative. If you find conflict with different characters in the movie focus on the character you feel most invested in.

items.short_description: It was important and relevant for the goals or needs of somebody
items.instructions: Important and relevant for the goals or needs of somebody is a situation that will help somebody achieve their wants and needs. Move the gauge up in situations that are important and relevant for somebodys goals and down for situations that are irrelevant. If you find conflict with different characters in the movie focus on the character you feel most invested in.
Controlled is an event that could have been averted or stopped. Move the gauge up the more controlled you perceive the situation and down as the situation is less controlled i.e. uncontrolled.
items.note: 按“可控性的多少”判为单极；不可控/可控也可被描述为相对状态，作者未给正式单/双极标签。

items.instructions: An event is predictable and could have been forseen. Move the gauge up the more predictable you perceive the situation to be an down for situations that are unpredictable.
items.note: 按“可预测性的多少”判为单极；这是连续属性，非两种独立情绪。

items.instructions: A sudden event occurred without much lead up or warning, the situation changed from one moment to another. Move the gauge up the more surprising and sudden an event occurred.

Rate the degree to which the event is caused by a human agent (including personified animals and machines) versus caused by chance. Move the gauge up the more you think the event was caused by a human agent and down the more it is caused by change. Use the middle of the scale if influences are even or if the cause was neither human nor chance.
items.note: 偶然原因与人类原因的来源对照，不是正负情绪；说明允许混合或既非两者时使用中间。

items.short_description: There was no urgency in the situation
items.instructions: There is urgency in the situation to act. Move up the gauge to indicate that there is urgency in the situation, move it down if the situation is not urgent.
You press your lips together. Move the gauge up to indicate pressing your lips together. When your lips are relaxed move the gauge down.

items.short_description: You had tears in your eyes
items.instructions: You have tears in your eyes, feel your eyes tearing up. Move the gauge up as you perceive tearing in your eyes. Move it down if your eyes are dry, that is no more tears than usual.

items.short_description: You felt your eyebrows go up
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel your eyebrows go up. Move it down as your eyebrows are relaxed in their normal position.
Move the gauge up as you observe yourself smiling. Move it down as you are not smiling.
Move the gauge up as you observe yourself frowning. Move it down as you are not frowning.

items.short_description: You felt the urge to stop what was happening
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel the urge to intervene and stop what is happening. Move it down if you do not feel an urge to stop what is happening.

items.short_description: You wanted to undo what was happening
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel the desire to undo what is happening. Move it down as you do not feel an urge to undo what is happening.

items.short_description: You wanted the ongoing situation to last or be repeated
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you want the ongoing situation to last or be repeated. Move it down if you don't want it to last or be repeated. You may use the middle of the scale if you are indifferent with respects to the situation to last or be repeated.
items.note: 暂按端点判为单极。说明同时把中间称为无所谓，故不能仅据两端确定心理学上严格的单极性。

items.short_description: You wanted to oppose someone or something (situation)
items.instructions: Move the gauge up if you want to oppose someone, something or the situation as a whole. Move the gauge down if you do not feel an urge to oppose someone or something.

items.short_description: You felt motivated to pay attention to what was going on
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel more motivated to pay attention to what was going on. Move it down if you feel disinterested in paying attention. You may use the middle of the scale if you feel indifferent with respect to the situation being repeated.
items.note: 暂按“不感兴趣↔注意被吸引”判为状态对照双极；说明末句误提重复事件，疑为复制残留。

items.short_description: You felt like tackling the situation and do something
items.instructions: Move the gauge up if you feel like tackling the situation and doing something. Move it down as you do not feel an urge to takle the situation.

items.short_description: You wanted to be in command of others
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you want command others. Move it down as you do not feel an urge to be in command of others.

items.short_description: You wanted someone to be there to provide help or support
items.instructions: Move the gauge up if you want someone to be there to provide help or support. Move it down as you do not feel the desire for someone to be there for support or help. You may use the middle of the scale if you are indifferent with regards to someone being there to provide help and support.
items.note: 暂按“无帮助愿望→有帮助愿望”判为单极；说明亦把中间称为中性，存在解释张力。

items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel like you want to move. Move it down as you do not feel an urge to move.

items.short_description: You wanted to take care of another person or cause
items.instructions: Move the gauge up if you want to take care of another person or cause. Move it down as you do not feel the urge to take care of another person or cause.
Move the gauge up as you feel bad. Move it down as you feel less bad.
items.note: 补表Lower Pole和Upper Pole均为Feel Bad，原文自相矛盾。本图按详细说明“向上更难受、向下较少难受”显示中文端点，未把推断冒充原始端点。

items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel good. Move it down as you feel less good.

Calm is the response to quiet and peaceful conditions. For example, you may experience calm when you are in a safe situation. Move the gauge up as you feel more calm. Move it down if you feel more restless.
Move the gauge up as you feel strong. Move it down as you feel weak. You may use the middle of the scale to indicate feeling neither particularly strong nor weak.

items.short_description: You experienced an intense emotional state
items.instructions: Move up the gauge as you experience an intense emotional state. Move it down as you do not feel intense emotions.
Move the gauge up as you feel alert and attentive. Move it down as you feel tired. You may use the middle of the scale to describe a level of alertnes that is 'normal' for you.
Move the gauge up as you feel at ease. Move it down as you feel more nervous. You may use the middle of the scale to indicate a state of neither feeling particularly at ease nor feeling nervous.

Move the gauge up as you experience muscle tensions in your whole body. Move it down as you experience your muscles relaxing. You may use the middle of the scale for what you perceive as your normal level of muscle tension.
items.note: 按“放松基线→紧张增加”暂判单极；详细说明又允许“中间为正常”，严格单/双极性质需额外确认。

items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you experience your heartbeat going faster. Move it down as you experience your heartbeat going slower. You may use the middle of the scale for what you perceive as your normal heartrate.
items.note: 这是对自己心跳的主观感觉，不是仪器测得的脉搏。该项未纳入扫描组48项片后验证。

items.short_description: You had a feeling of a lump in the throat
items.instructions: Move the gauge up as you feel a lump in your throat. Move it down as your throat feels clear as usual.
Move the gauge up as you feel discomfort in your stomach. Move it down as your stomach feels comfortable as normal.
Move the gauge up as you felt physically warm. Move it down if you feel physically cold. You may use the middle of the scale to describe feeling at a temperature that is 'normal' for you.
items.note: 这是主观冷热感觉。该项未纳入扫描组48项片后验证。

items.instructions: Anger is a feeling of irritation or rage towards another person or situation. Move up the gauge as you feel increasing anger. Move it down as you do not feel angry.

Guilt is the response when a person regrets having violated agreements, principles, or values. For example, you may experience guilt when some behaviours or situations violate your own values or moral code. Move the gauge up as you feel guity. Move it down as you feel less guilty.

Warm-hearted is a feeling of sympathy, affection, kindness, and cordiality for situations or people. For example, you may experience warm-hearted when you witness an event that you find very positive and comforting. Move the gauge up as you feel more warm-hearted. Move it down if you do not feel warm-hearted towards the situation or the people in it.

Disgust is the response to sights, situations, and actions that we do not accept. For example, you may experience disgust when someone behaves in a way that you disapprove. Move the gauge up as you feel disgusted. Move it down as you do not feel disgusted.
Happiness is a feeling of joy opposite to feeling sad. Move the gauge up as you feel more happy. Move it down as you feel less happy.
items.note: 定义句提到sad，但显示端点是Not Happy→Happy；不据此改成悲伤↔快乐。

items.instructions: Fear is the response to concrete physical and psychological threats. For example, you may experience fear when your/someone’s life, health, or well-being is threatened. Move up the gauge as you feel fearful. Move it down as you feel less fearful.

Regard is a feeling of respect and sympathy towards another person. Opposite to regard; contempt is a feeling of moral superiority, disrespect, and aversion towards another person. Move the gauge up as you feel regard. Move it down as you feel contempt. You may use the middle of the scale if you feel neither regard nor contemt.

Anxiety is a feeling of tension, apprehension, worry, and nervousness. For example, you may experience anxiety when you worry about something that is happening or might happen in the future. Move up the gauge as you feel more anxious. Move it down as you feel less anxious.

Satisfaction is the response to the fulfilment of our wishes, expectations, and needs. Move the gauge up as you feel more satisfied. Move it down as you feel dissatisfied. You may use the middle of the scale to describe a neutral state of being neither satisfied nor dissatisfied.

Pride is a feeling of pleasure or satisfaction with ones achievements. Shame is a feeling of humiliation or distress when a person is conscious of their wrongdoings or faults. Move the gauge up as you feel more proud. Move it down as you feel more ashamed. You may use the middle of the scale if you feel neither pride nor shame.

Surprise is the response to sudden expected events. For example, you may experience surprise when you are in unusual situations or someone acts unexpectedly. Move the gauge up as you feel more surprised. Move it down as you feel less surprise.

Love is a strong feeling of liking some people very much and being attached to them. For example, you may experience love when you like a person, a child, or a lover very much. Move the gauge up as you feel more love. Move it down as you feel less love.
Sadness is the response to the loss of an object or a person to which you are attached. Move the gauge up as you feel more sad. Move it down as you do not feel sad
